blocks.orig: Tanzania is the place to be for those who love travel and adventure. This beautiful East African country, which borders the Indian Ocean, has something for everyone. Large cities and untouched landscapes means you don’t need to leave this sunny oasis to fulfill your vacation desires.
blocks.html: If you love travel and adventure, Tanzania is where you want to be. This lovely East African country on the Indian Ocean has something to offer every kind of traveller. Between its big cities and untouched landscapes, you can fulfil all your holiday wishes without ever leaving this sunny oasis.

blocks.orig: To help you plan the perfect trip, we have advice on how to plan, where to go, and tricks to help you get the most out of your travels.
blocks.html: To help you put together the ideal trip, we share advice on planning, on where to go and on tricks that help you make the most of your travels.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is the land of extremes. It is situated 600 feet (or 200 meters) above sea level and contains both the tallest mountain in Africa and the second deepest lake in the world. That’s right, Kilimanjaro, which is measured at 19,340 feet (or 5,895 meters), lives in this country.
blocks.html: Tanzania is a country of extremes. It lies 600 feet (or 200 metres) above sea level and is home to both Africa’s highest mountain and the world’s second deepest lake. Indeed, Kilimanjaro, measuring 19,340 feet (or 5,895 metres), stands in this country.

blocks.orig: The world’s second deepest lake is Lake Tanganyika, which measures 4,710 feet (or 1,436 meters). The gold medal goes to Lake Baikal in Russia which measures 5,387 feet (or 1,642 meters), creating a large gap between first and second place.
blocks.html: Lake Tanganyika, at 4,710 feet (or 1,436 metres), is the second deepest lake on earth. First place belongs to Russia’s Lake Baikal at 5,387 feet (or 1,642 metres), which leaves a big gap between the two.

blocks.orig: But just because these are the most famous parts of the country, doesn’t mean they are the only joys you can experience.
blocks.html: Still, the fact that these are the country’s best-known features does not mean they are the only delights you can enjoy.

blocks.orig: In 1964, the mainland called Tanganyika and the islands called Zanzibar unified. It was at this point that the United Republic of Tanzania was born.
blocks.html: In 1964, the mainland, Tanganyika, joined with the islands of Zanzibar. That union marked the birth of the United Republic of Tanzania.

blocks.orig: The merger wasn’t possible until both countries became independent from the British. Tanganyika reached independence in 1961, while Zanzibar only managed the feat in January 1964. 3 months later, Tanzania became united.
blocks.html: The union could only happen once both countries had gained independence from Britain. Tanganyika became independent in 1961, whereas Zanzibar only achieved it in January 1964. Three months after that, Tanzania was united.

blocks.orig: The country of Tanzania is known as “the Cradle of Mankind” as it holds the oldest human fossils in the world. With 120 different indigenous groups in the country, and very little emigration or colonial settlement in their history, Tanzania has kept a lot of its original history intact.
blocks.html: Because it holds the oldest human fossils in the world, Tanzania is called “the Cradle of Mankind”. The country has 120 different indigenous groups, and as there was very little emigration or colonial settlement in its past, much of its original history has been preserved.

blocks.orig: There are two official languages in Tanzania – English, and Swahili. Although English is spoken by many people in the country, it is only taught in higher education. Swahili is taught in the first 7 years of education and continues until the end of a pupil’s schooling.
blocks.html: Tanzania has two official languages – Swahili and English. Many people in the country speak English, but it is only taught in higher education. Swahili is taught from the first 7 years of school right through to the end of a pupil’s education.

blocks.orig: Because the country is so vast and diverse in culture, there are many unofficial languages spoken by the locals too. For example, many of the 120 ethnic groups have their own language, and due to Asian influences Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi, and Gujarati have become popular.
blocks.html: As the country is so large and culturally varied, locals also speak many unofficial languages. Many of the 120 ethnic groups have a language of their own, for instance, and Asian influences have made Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi and Gujarati widely spoken.

blocks.orig: The concept of kin and family is critical to Tanzania’s culture. No matter the struggle or inconvenience, family matters and occasions are given the highest priority. The transport system in Tanzania has much to be desired, but that won’t stop a family member from arriving for a celebration.
blocks.html: Family and kinship are central to Tanzania’s culture. Whatever the difficulty or inconvenience, family matters and events always come first. Transport in Tanzania leaves a lot to be desired, yet that will not keep a relative from turning up for a celebration.

blocks.orig: Art and history are also extremely important in Tanzania’s culture. Storytelling through dance and speech creates the majority of entertainment. And because scientists from around the world sturdy human ancestry in Tanzania soil, the concept of history and nature are woven into one.
blocks.html: Art and history also matter greatly in Tanzania’s culture. Most entertainment comes from storytelling through speech and dance. And since scientists from all over the world study human ancestry in Tanzanian soil, history and nature are closely intertwined.

blocks.orig: The most important elements of planning a visit to Tanzania are the weather and the experience.
blocks.html: When you plan a trip to Tanzania, the two key things to consider are the weather and the experience you want.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is a country surrounded by wildlife, beaches, archaeological discoveries, and a culture largely untainted by globalization.
blocks.html: Tanzania is full of wildlife, beaches and archaeological finds, with a culture that globalisation has largely left untouched.

blocks.orig: We will go into detail about the things you can do while visiting this unique country, but the main reason to spend time in Tanzania is to explore the untouched world.
blocks.html: Later on we go into detail about what you can do in this unique country, but the main reason to spend time in Tanzania is to discover a world that is still untouched.

blocks.orig: Many places like Katavi, contain wilderness that hasn’t been destroyed by progress or time. It is the ultimate escape from a fast-paced life.
blocks.html: In many places, such as Katavi, you will find wilderness that neither progress nor time has spoiled. It is the perfect escape from a hectic life.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has two seasons – wet and dry. The rainy season starts near the end of October and continues until January. It picks up again from March to June. Between these bouts of rain, is the dry season.
blocks.html: There are two seasons in Tanzania – dry and wet. The rains begin towards the end of October and last until January. They return from March to June. In between these rainy spells comes the dry season.

blocks.orig: Visiting in the dry season (February, then July till September), means climbing mountains in a safe condition, and exploring areas in the beautiful sun of 77 degrees Fahrenheit (25 degrees Celsius). The roads will be easier to drive on and the wildlife will be around waterholes making them easier to spot.
blocks.html: If you travel in the dry season (February, and then July to September), you can climb mountains in safe conditions and explore in lovely sunshine of 77 degrees Fahrenheit (25 degrees Celsius). Driving on the roads is easier, and the animals gather around waterholes, which makes them easier to find.

blocks.orig: However, if you want to see large movements of animals, you can also do this during the rainy season. The rain makes the wildlife happy, while the grassland will be colorful and luscious. You will develop the best photos and see a large variety of creatures. The experience will also be at its cheapest with fewer crowds to contend with.
blocks.html: That said, the rainy season is also a good time to watch large movements of animals. The wildlife thrives on the rain, and the grassland turns lush and colourful. You will take your best photos and see a wide range of animals. It is also the least expensive time to travel and there are fewer crowds to deal with.

blocks.orig: There are areas that can’t be reached in the rainy season, but the whole northern circuit will normally be accessible throughout the year.
blocks.html: Some areas can’t be reached during the rainy season, but the entire northern circuit is usually open all year round.

blocks.orig: Yes. To travel to Tanzania, you will need a passport, a return ticket, and a single-entry tourist visa. This is true for most countries, although you can check your country’s status on this link.
blocks.html: Yes. If you want to visit Tanzania, you need a passport, a return ticket and a single-entry tourist visa. This applies to most countries, but you can check the rules for your own country’s citizens via this link.

blocks.orig: The passport should be valid for at least 6 months before your arrival date, but the visa can be obtained at the airport.
blocks.html: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months before the date you arrive, while the visa can be arranged at the airport.

blocks.orig: Although you can wait until the last minute to receive your visa, this can cause delays and rejection. We advise applying for the visa in advance to avoid any raised prices and long waiting times with the immigration officers.
blocks.html: You can leave your visa until the very last moment, but doing so may lead to delays or a refusal. We suggest applying in advance so you avoid higher prices and long queues at immigration.

blocks.orig: Ideally, your Tanzania safari should be at least 10 days long. 10 days is enough to travel across the Northern Circuit (Serengeti, Tarangire, and Ngorongoro) which is the most popular safari in Africa.
blocks.html: Your safari in Tanzania should ideally last at least 10 days. That gives you enough time to cover the Northern Circuit (Serengeti, Tarangire and Ngorongoro), the most popular safari route in Africa.

blocks.orig: With a longer stay, you can also include visits to the lakes and cultural hubs in the area.
blocks.html: If you stay longer, you can add the lakes and the cultural centres of the region as well.

blocks.orig: Before traveling to Tanzania, it’s recommended to ask for advice about the following vaccinations:
blocks.html: Before you travel to Tanzania, it is a good idea to seek advice on the vaccinations below:

blocks.orig: If you are staying for longer than two weeks, some doctors recommend getting vaccinated for Typhoid. And if you are interacting with animals directly, (such as petting or working on a farm) some doctors recommend to include rabies vaccinations.
blocks.html: For stays of more than two weeks, some doctors advise a Typhoid vaccination. And if you will be in direct contact with animals (for example petting them or working on a farm), some doctors suggest adding rabies vaccinations.

blocks.orig: Speak to your doctor about what vaccinations you have already received, as many people have protection against illnesses such as meningitis during their childhood.
blocks.html: Talk to your doctor about the vaccinations you have already had, since many people were protected against diseases such as meningitis as children.

blocks.orig: The national currency of Tanzania is the Tanzanian Shilling. It is often written as with TSh or /=. Coins come in 50s, 100s, and 200s, and notes come in 500s, 1000s, and 5000s.
blocks.html: Tanzania’s national currency is the Tanzanian Shilling, often shown as TSh or /=. Coins come in 50s, 100s and 200s, while notes come in 500s, 1000s and 5000s.

blocks.orig: Most towns will exchange US Dollars, UK pound Sterling and European Euros without issue. However, you may notice that US Dollars and Euros are accepted in large areas of the country.
blocks.html: In most towns you can change US Dollars, UK pounds Sterling and European Euros without any trouble. You may also find that US Dollars and Euros are accepted across large parts of the country.

blocks.orig: As of July 2022, USD$100 is worth TSh233,200, £100 is worth TSh277,949,91 and €100 is worth TSh234,704.14.
blocks.html: In July 2022, USD$100 was worth TSh233,200, £100 was worth TSh277,949,91 and €100 was worth TSh234,704.14.

blocks.orig: There is tons to do in Tanzania, but they all come down to three things – exploring the wilderness, finding wild animals, and discovering the culture of the area.
blocks.html: You can do lots in Tanzania, but it all boils down to three things – discovering the local culture, searching for wild animals and exploring the wilderness.

blocks.orig: The Big 5 is a tick box exercise that lets you see the most iconic animals in Africa. Going on Big 5 safaris means searching for the African Lion, the African Elephant, the African Leopard, the Rhinoceros, and the Cape Buffalo.
blocks.html: The Big 5 is a checklist of Africa’s most iconic animals. On a Big 5 safari you look for the African Lion, the African Elephant, the African Leopard, the Rhinoceros and the Cape Buffalo.

blocks.orig: Although these creatures are large, they can be extremely difficult to spot in the wild. The goal becomes even more difficult due to illegal poachers reducing the numbers of the population. However, hiring a Big 5 tour guide can show you the best places to find these extraordinary animals.
blocks.html: Big as these animals are, they can be very hard to find in the wild. Illegal poaching, which reduces their numbers, makes the task harder still. A Big 5 tour guide, however, can take you to the best spots to see these remarkable animals.

blocks.orig: The great migration is the iconic trek made by thousands of wildebeest to cross the lands of Africa. It has been watched millions of times through hundreds of documentaries, but there is nothing like seeing a surreal experience in real life.
blocks.html: The great migration is the famous journey that thousands of wildebeest make across the plains of Africa. Millions of people have seen it in hundreds of documentaries, yet nothing compares with witnessing this surreal sight in person.

blocks.orig: The wildebeest migration is the largest mammal migration in the world, and you can see the spectical in the Serengeti National Park.
blocks.html: No mammal migration in the world is larger than the wildebeest migration, and you can watch this spectacle in Serengeti National Park.

blocks.orig: Mount Kilimanjaro National Park is unlike the other national parks in Tanzania. You won’t find a lot of wildlife on this tour, instead, the attraction is climbing Kilimanjaro, the tallest mountain in Africa.
blocks.html: Mount Kilimanjaro National Park differs from Tanzania’s other national parks. Wildlife is scarce on this tour; the real draw is the climb up Kilimanjaro, Africa’s highest mountain.

blocks.orig: Even if you don’t reach the summit, the view of the wilderness below is a sight for the gods.
blocks.html: Even if you do not make it to the top, the view over the wilderness below is truly heavenly.

blocks.orig: Go On A Safari To Serengeti National Park
blocks.html: Take a safari in Serengeti National Park

blocks.orig: Even if you aren’t traveling for the Big 5 or to spot the great migration, you should still visit Serengeti National Park. It is the second largest national park in Tanzania and is home to over 500 species of birds, and millions of grazing animals such as zebras and gazelles on flat land for easy viewing.
blocks.html: Even if the Big 5 or the great migration are not your reason for travelling, Serengeti National Park is still worth a visit. It is Tanzania’s second largest national park, with more than 500 bird species and millions of grazing animals such as gazelles and zebras on open, flat land where they are easy to see.

blocks.orig: The Northern Circuit contains the most famous national parks in Tanzania. As we said before, you can visit national parks such as Serengeti, Tarangire, and Ngorongoro. But you can also explore Arusha, Lake Manyara, Lake Eyasi, Lake Natron, Kilimanjaro, Olduvai, and Mkomazi.
blocks.html: Tanzania’s best-known national parks lie on the Northern Circuit. As mentioned earlier, you can visit parks such as Serengeti, Tarangire and Ngorongoro. You can also explore Arusha, Lake Manyara, Lake Eyasi, Lake Natron, Kilimanjaro, Olduvai and Mkomazi.

blocks.orig: Traveling the entire area can take you around 10 days, and in that time you’ll spot animals in their natural habitat.
blocks.html: Covering the whole region takes about 10 days, during which you will see animals in their natural surroundings.

blocks.orig: If you don’t have the time to dictate 10 days of endless plains travel, you can experience the whole area much quicker by skipping some parts or to make use of flights in safaris! Don’t let time keep you from enjoying all that Tanzania has to offer. Imagine yourself doing an amazing safari or overlooking the endless plains from a hot air balloon!
blocks.html: If you cannot set aside 10 days for travelling across the endless plains, you can see the whole region far more quickly by leaving out some parts or by using flights on your safari! Don’t let a lack of time stop you from enjoying everything Tanzania has to offer. Picture yourself on a wonderful safari, or gazing over the endless plains from a hot air balloon!

blocks.orig: If you’re not near the northern park of Tanzania, don’t fret. There are 35 national parks around the country. North, East, South, and West. Each has its own highlights and attractions, so search for the park close to your hotel destination and create your wildlife experience from there.
blocks.html: Not close to Tanzania’s northern parks? No need to worry. The country has 35 national parks spread across the north, east, south and west. Each one has its own highlights and attractions, so look for a park near your hotel and plan your wildlife experience from there.

blocks.orig: Stone Town is considered the architectural capital of Tanzania. Found on the island of Zanzibar, the majority of homes in the area were built in the 19th century. The wooden doors on the houses are often beautifully carved and delicately maintained.
blocks.html: Stone Town is regarded as Tanzania’s architectural capital. Located on the island of Zanzibar, most of its houses date from the 19th century. Their wooden doors are often beautifully carved and carefully looked after.

blocks.orig: Stone Town is the oldest functioning town in the world, which makes it a wonderful place for history lovers. The cultures of the area haven’t changed, allowing us to see culture and history in action.
blocks.html: As the oldest functioning town in the world, Stone Town is a great place for anyone who loves history. Local cultures have stayed the same, so you can see culture and history come alive.

blocks.orig: One of the best places to dive in Tanzania is the Zanzibar island called Pemba. Its white sand beach is often untouched, and the clear waters make it perfect for scuba diving.
blocks.html: Pemba, a Zanzibar island, is one of Tanzania’s top diving spots. Its white sandy beach is often deserted, and the clear water makes it ideal for scuba diving.

blocks.orig: The area is laid back and the island is so hilly that spending a weekend swimming and then mountain biking has become a popular activity.
blocks.html: Life here is relaxed, and the island is so hilly that a weekend of swimming followed by mountain biking has become a popular pastime.

blocks.orig: The Mafia Island has the same beautiful beaches as Pemba, and the same almost see-through water. However, on Mafia Island, you can experience the Marine Park. This is a coral garden found just off the water’s edge. You can witness over 400 species of bright and colorful fish, dancing around the coral reef.
blocks.html: Mafia Island has beaches just as beautiful as Pemba’s and the same almost transparent water. On Mafia Island, though, you can also visit the Marine Park, a coral garden lying just off the shore. You can see more than 400 species of bright, colourful fish darting around the coral reef.

blocks.orig: This island is also the traditional breeding ground for the endangered green turtle. Making it one of the only safe havens for the rare species.
blocks.html: The island is also a traditional breeding ground for the endangered green turtle, which makes it one of the few safe havens for this rare species.

blocks.orig: Rift Valley got its name due to the earth’s weakened crust. The area is a geological phenomenon, as the valley cracks down for thousands of miles. The dramatic drop has created naturally hot springs, volcanoes, lakes, and geysers.
blocks.html: The Rift Valley owes its name to the earth’s weakened crust. It is a geological phenomenon, with the valley splitting the land for thousands of miles. This steep drop has produced natural hot springs, lakes, volcanoes and geysers.

blocks.orig: It’s in this valley that flamingos find a home, and baboons rule the roost. The rift itself runs from Syria to Mozambique and the tectonic plates are slowly making the split larger, year after year. In some places the top of the rift valley will reach 400 meters and has a very steep drop. The view from the top of this valley is amazing. One of the most popular locations on the top of this Rift valley is Manyara Best View lodge, a real attraction that is often combined with Tarangire, Ngorongoro or Lake Manyara national park.
blocks.html: This valley is where flamingos make their home and baboons are in charge. The rift stretches from Syria to Mozambique, and the tectonic plates widen the split a little more every year. In places the top of the rift valley reaches 400 metres, with a very sheer drop. The view from up there is stunning. A favourite spot at the top of the Rift valley is Manyara Best View lodge, a real attraction that is often paired with Tarangire, Ngorongoro or Lake Manyara national park.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has over 14 large lakes around the country. The smallest surface area is Lake Chala which borders Tanzania and Kenya. It measures 4.2 kilometers squared or 1.6 square miles.
blocks.html: There are more than 14 large lakes across Tanzania. Lake Chala, on the border between Tanzania and Kenya, has the smallest surface area, at 4.2 square kilometres or 1.6 square miles.

blocks.orig: The largest surface area is claimed by Lake Victoria measuring 68,800 kilometers squared, or 26,600 square miles. For comparison, the United Kingdom is 243,610 kilometers squared, and Scotland is 77,910 kilometers square. Meaning the lake named after Queen Victoria is the same size as one of her countries.
blocks.html: Lake Victoria has the largest surface area, at 68,800 square kilometres, or 26,600 square miles. To put that in perspective, the United Kingdom covers 243,610 square kilometres and Scotland 77,910 square kilometres. So the lake named after Queen Victoria is about as big as one of her countries.

blocks.orig: Although this lake is only the second largest lake in the world. It is the largest tropical lake by miles.
blocks.html: It is only the second largest lake in the world, but by a long way it is the largest tropical lake.

blocks.orig: The lake itself is so large that it touches on three countries – Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.
blocks.html: The lake is so big that it borders three countries – Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

blocks.orig: It was named after Queen Victoria in 1858 and contains fish you’ll find nowhere else on earth.
blocks.html: It was given Queen Victoria’s name in 1858 and is home to fish found nowhere else in the world.

blocks.orig: Lake Manyara is best known for its birds. You can find over a million flamingos, thousands of pelicans, hundreds of storks, and even rare creatures such as the chestnut-banded plover.
blocks.html: Lake Manyara is famous above all for its birdlife. More than a million flamingos live here, along with thousands of pelicans, hundreds of storks and even rare species such as the chestnut-banded plover.

blocks.orig: The fish are mostly carp, so we would recommend this lake for bird lovers over fish lovers.
blocks.html: Most of the fish are carp, so we suggest this lake to bird lovers rather than fish lovers.

blocks.orig: To reach this lake, you’ll be taken on a jeep that goes through the wild forest and shrublands to reach the marsh. The travel and backdrop are jaw-dropping.
blocks.html: You travel to the lake by jeep, driving through wild forest and shrubland until you reach the marsh. Both the journey and the scenery are breathtaking.

blocks.orig: You are allowed to fish in this lake as you watch the flamingos fly by.
blocks.html: Fishing is permitted on the lake, so you can cast a line while flamingos fly past.

blocks.orig: Natron is an alkaline lake with a pH level of 12 or more. Scientists believe this high alkaline level comes from lava underneath the water which produces large amounts of carbonate.
blocks.html: Natron is an alkaline lake with a pH of 12 or higher. According to scientists, this high alkalinity is caused by lava beneath the water that releases large quantities of carbonate.

blocks.orig: Because of the unusual alkaline disposition, salt-loving plants and animals live in these waters. Instead of using green pigments for photosynthesis, these flowers are almost all red. This creates an illusion of a blood lake.
blocks.html: Thanks to this unusual alkaline character, the water is home to plants and animals that thrive in salt. Rather than green pigments for photosynthesis, almost all of these flowers use red ones, which makes the lake look as if it is full of blood.

blocks.orig: Flamingos eat the redfish, animals, and plant life helping them create a red and pink tone in their feathers.
blocks.html: The flamingos feed on the redfish, animals and plants, which gives their feathers a red and pink colour.

blocks.orig: Reaching this area can be very difficult due to the lack of roads, a professional guide has the knowledge on how to reach this place best. But Lake Natron cant be accessed during the rainy season.
blocks.html: Getting here can be very hard because there are hardly any roads, but a professional guide knows the best way to reach it. Lake Natron can’t be visited in the rainy season, however.

blocks.orig: This lake is less of an animal reserve and more of a sporting experience. You can hike to the area, have a canoe in the waters, and cycle around the waterways. Swimming is prohibited, but the area allows for gentle water sports while you take in the beautiful scenery.
blocks.html: Rather than a wildlife reserve, this lake is more of a place for sport. You can hike there, paddle a canoe on the water and cycle along the waterways. Swimming is not allowed, but gentle water sports are, so you can enjoy them while taking in the lovely scenery.

blocks.orig: Lake Momella is actually made up of 7 lakes. Big Momela, Small Momelaa, Tulusia, Lekandrio, El Kekhotoito, Rishateni and Kusare.
blocks.html: Lake Momella in fact consists of 7 lakes: Big Momela, Small Momelaa, Tulusia, Lekandrio, El Kekhotoito, Rishateni and Kusare.

blocks.orig: They are all shallow alkaline lakes that are perfect for flamingo watching. You can also expect pelicans, guinea fowl, African fish eagles, Egyptian geese, and African jacanas in these lakes.
blocks.html: Each of them is a shallow alkaline lake, ideal for watching flamingos. You are also likely to see pelicans, guinea fowl, African fish eagles, Egyptian geese and African jacanas here.

blocks.orig: Most mammals don’t drink from this lake due to the high alkaline content, however, you can spot zebras, waterbucks, and giraffes in the surrounding areas too.
blocks.html: Because of the high alkalinity, most mammals do not drink the water, but you can still see giraffes, waterbucks and zebras in the area around the lakes.

blocks.orig: To really enjoy the experience, you should take a canoe trip to travel around the lakes.
blocks.html: For the best experience, go on a canoe trip to get around the lakes.

blocks.orig: If you prefer an active vacation instead of an animal-watching one, then we suggest finding a surfing beach in the islands of Zanzibar. The white sand beaches, and clear shallow water, makes learning the sport easy.
blocks.html: If an active holiday appeals to you more than one spent watching animals, we suggest looking for a surf beach on the Zanzibar islands. With white sandy beaches and clear, shallow water, it is easy to learn the sport here.

blocks.orig: You can also hire boats to explore the clear ocean water while staying close to the island’s land.
blocks.html: You can also rent a boat to explore the clear sea while staying near the island’s shore.

blocks.orig: The Iraqw tribe is an ancient community that lives in the same way they did over 100 years ago.
blocks.html: The Iraqw tribe is an ancient community that still lives just as it did more than 100 years ago.

blocks.orig: Over 150 tribes live and thrive in the country of Tanzania, but the Iraqw tribe allows visitors to experience their way of life. You can talk to the residents, enter their homes and join in on their agriculture.
blocks.html: More than 150 tribes live and flourish in Tanzania, but the Iraqw tribe gives visitors the chance to share in their way of life. You can chat with the villagers, step inside their homes and take part in their farming.

blocks.orig: If you visit on the 7th or 25th day of the month, you can experience the Iraqw market. Here the people of the village sell their goods, from cattle to art, herbs to clothing. It would be a unique souvenir to take home.
blocks.html: Visit on the 7th or the 25th of the month and you can see the Iraqw market, where villagers sell everything from cattle to art and from herbs to clothing. It makes for a one-of-a-kind souvenir to bring home.

blocks.orig: In the Maasai Village, you can expect the same raw culture as the Iraqw Village. However, the Maasai people continue to live in the heart of Africa. There are lions, and elephants roaming their lands, but they aren’t afraid of these deadly creatures.
blocks.html: At the Maasai Village, you will find the same authentic culture as in the Iraqw Village. The Maasai, however, still live in the heart of Africa. Lions and elephants roam their land, yet they do not fear these dangerous animals.

blocks.orig: Instead, the Maasai people know how to live in harmony with nature – a skill they could pass on to you.
blocks.html: Rather, the Maasai know how to live in balance with nature – something they may be able to teach you.

blocks.orig: We have mentioned the Ngorongoro National Park a couple of times, because it is so special. It is known as one of the 7 African wonders. It has the highest concentration of wildlife per square kilometer. And perfect circumstances for the wildlife to live.
blocks.html: We have brought up Ngorongoro National Park several times because it is so special. It is called one of the 7 African wonders, has the highest density of wildlife per square kilometre and offers ideal conditions for animals to live in.

blocks.orig: The crater creates a permanent supply of water for the animals, allowing us to see the beautiful creatures flock to the watering hole.
blocks.html: The crater provides a year-round water supply for the animals, so you can watch these lovely creatures gather at the waterhole.

blocks.orig: The crater itself is around a million years old and was once one of the tallest mountains in the world before its destructive explosion. It has been higher than Mt. Kilimanjaro and due to the volcanic eruption this amazing area has been created. It is actually not a crater, but a caldera. But it is known as Ngorongoro Crater.
blocks.html: The crater is roughly a million years old and was once among the highest mountains in the world, until a devastating explosion. It was taller than Mt. Kilimanjaro, and this remarkable landscape was formed by the volcanic eruption. Strictly speaking it is a caldera rather than a crater, but it is known as Ngorongoro Crater.

blocks.orig: Explore The Arusha Cultural Heritage Center
blocks.html: Visit the Arusha Cultural Heritage Center

blocks.orig: The Arusha Cultural Heritage Center is filled with African art from across the continent. You can find masks, furniture, statues, and crafts, displayed with the history of active and long past tribes.
blocks.html: African art from all over the continent fills the Arusha Cultural Heritage Center. Masks, statues, furniture and crafts are on show, together with the history of tribes both living and long gone.

blocks.orig: One particular gem you will learn about is the Tanzanite. Named after its one known source, Tanzania, this gem can only be found in Mirerani Hills.
blocks.html: One gem in particular you will hear about is Tanzanite. It takes its name from Tanzania, its only known source, and is found solely in the Mirerani Hills.

blocks.orig: The desire to find such a rare and beautiful gem created wars in countries around the world. You can learn about the impact this gem had on Tanzania and the surrounding countries.
blocks.html: The longing for such a rare and lovely stone sparked wars in countries all over the world. Here you can find out what impact the gem has had on Tanzania and its neighbours.

blocks.orig: The Olduvai Gorge is a historical archaeological site that you can visit. The oldest human bones have been found in the area, including skulls aged around 2 million years old.
blocks.html: You can visit the Olduvai Gorge, a historic archaeological site. The oldest human bones ever found come from this area, among them skulls of around 2 million years old.

blocks.orig: If you visit between June and October, you may be able to talk to an active archaeologist digging on the site. They can tell you what they have found recently and what that means in terms of knowledge about our ancestors.
blocks.html: Between June and October you may get the chance to speak with an archaeologist working at the site. They can explain their latest finds and what these reveal about our ancestors.

blocks.orig: If there are no active archaeologists, you can still talk to the tour guides and visit the museum to take home replicas.
blocks.html: If no archaeologists are at work, you can still chat with the tour guides and visit the museum, where you can buy replicas to take home.

blocks.orig: If you want a hotel that gives you 5-star treatment and is close to the animals you’ll explore during the day. Then you should stay at Singita Faru Faru Lodge or Melia Serengeti Lodge. It is situated on the outskirts of the National Park, allowing you the most beautiful views as the sun sets on the plains.
blocks.html: Would you like a hotel with 5-star service near the animals you will be exploring during the day? Then stay at Singita Faru Faru Lodge or Melia Serengeti Lodge. It lies on the edge of the National Park, giving you gorgeous views as the sun goes down over the plains.

blocks.orig: The hotel has a spa, a personal walking safari tour, a fine dining restaurant, and more. You can expect access to the outdoor pool, and to the hiking trails either with or without a guide.
blocks.html: The hotel offers a spa, a private walking safari, a fine dining restaurant and more. You can use the outdoor pool and the hiking trails, with or without a guide.

blocks.orig: If you would rather stay near the cultural hub of Tanzania, you can book with Legendary Lodge or Elewana Arusha Coffee Lodge. It is at the center of all activity in Arusha while keeping a cool and distant vibe inside.
blocks.html: Prefer to stay close to Tanzania’s cultural hub? Then book Legendary Lodge or Elewana Arusha Coffee Lodge. It sits right in the middle of everything happening in Arusha, yet feels calm and secluded inside.

blocks.orig: As a coffee-focused lodge, you can experience the best coffee from across the continent, alongside a fine dining experience and access to the spa and pool.
blocks.html: Since the lodge revolves around coffee, you can taste the best coffee from across the continent, as well as enjoy fine dining and use of the pool and spa.

blocks.orig: And lastly, if you prefer your hotel to act as an entertainment center in itself, then try Tulia Zanzibar, the best luxury romantic resort. With a private beach, scuba diving experiences, shows, and evening fine dining, you’ll need to be reminded that there is more outside of their doors.
blocks.html: Finally, if you would like your hotel to be a source of entertainment in its own right, try Tulia Zanzibar, the best romantic luxury resort. With its private beach, scuba diving, shows and fine dining in the evening, you may need reminding that there is more to see beyond its doors.

blocks.orig: If you want to enjoy your holiday in Zanzibar specifically, then we have a couple more hotels to suggest.
blocks.html: If your Zanzibar holiday is what you want to enjoy most, we have a few more hotels to recommend.

blocks.orig: The Residence Zanzibar is a secluded hideaway near the coastline of the ocean. There are 66 luxurious villas to choose from each with cultural comforts from around the world. Allowing you to pick options from your own country to try something new.
blocks.html: The Residence Zanzibar is a secluded retreat close to the ocean shore. You can choose from 66 luxurious villas, each with cultural comforts from around the globe, so you can pick something from your own country or try something new.

blocks.orig: Each room has a balcony, a private beach, ocean views, and access to the pool.
blocks.html: Every room comes with a balcony, ocean views, a private beach and use of the pool.

blocks.orig: Baraza Resort and Spa Zanzibar is a resort that brings heritage to your holiday. You can expect influences from Arabic as well as Swahili culture in the architecture. The beach is just on the doorstep and the food is divine.
blocks.html: Baraza Resort and Spa Zanzibar adds a sense of heritage to your holiday. Its architecture shows both Swahili and Arabic influences. The beach is right outside, and the food is heavenly.

blocks.orig: Hotel Riu Palace Zanzibar was recently renovated in 2019. They have pools, whirlpools, a spar, and entertainment for the evening and the day. The steakhouse produces 5-star food, and you can enjoy your stay while looking out onto the clear beach.
blocks.html: Hotel Riu Palace Zanzibar had a renovation not long ago, in 2019. It has pools, whirlpools, a spa and entertainment both during the day and in the evening. The steakhouse serves 5-star food, and you can enjoy your stay with a view over the clear beach.

blocks.orig: Before packing your bags, we have a couple of tips to give you. Whenever you travel to a new country, there will be cultural and practical differences that you need to be aware of.
blocks.html: Before you pack your bags, here are a few tips. Any time you visit a new country, there are cultural and practical differences worth knowing about.

blocks.orig: When you travel with us, you have access to a professional guide throughout your stay. With a professional guide, you’ll be able to find the hotspots for rare wildlife, and will have access to the more secure areas.
blocks.html: Travelling with us means you have a professional guide with you for your whole stay. A professional guide knows where to find rare wildlife and can take you into the more secure areas.

blocks.orig: Without a professional guide, you may miss out on the details and hard-to-find animals on the safaris.
blocks.html: Without one, you risk missing the finer details and the animals that are hard to find on safari.

blocks.orig: In the height of the dry season, Tanzania can become crowded. When there are more people than animals, it’s time to avoid the well-known paths. We suggest visiting Rubondo Island in the middle of Lake Victoria.
blocks.html: At the peak of the dry season, Tanzania can get busy. Once there are more people than animals, it is time to leave the familiar routes. We recommend a visit to Rubondo Island, in the middle of Lake Victoria.

blocks.orig: Imagine a Robinson Crusoe adventure, where the mountains are empty of people and the wildlife sanctuary continues as if humans never touched it.
blocks.html: Picture a Robinson Crusoe adventure, with mountains free of people and a wildlife sanctuary carrying on as though humans had never set foot there.

blocks.orig: There are multiple different airports in Tanzania, so don’t just fly to the capital city of Dar es Salaam and waste a day traveling to your hotel. There are airports just outside of Arusha, directly to Kilimanjaro, and easy connections to Serengeti.
blocks.html: Tanzania has several airports, so avoid flying into the capital, Dar es Salaam, only to lose a day getting to your hotel. There are airports just outside Arusha, direct ones to Kilimanjaro and easy connections to Serengeti.

blocks.orig: Check which options make the most sense for time and money, so you don’t waste either going with the capital.
blocks.html: Work out which options save you the most time and money, so you do not waste either by choosing the capital.

blocks.orig: To make sure you don’t get charged extra for using your phone abroad, you should buy a sim card locally. These sims will have better wifi and signal connections, and they will be cheaper due to their expected use in the country.
blocks.html: Buy a local SIM card so you are not charged extra for using your phone abroad. Local SIMs give you better wifi and signal, and they cost less because they are designed for use in the country.

blocks.orig: We recommend choosing Vodacom, Airtel, or Tigo. Airtel is a budget brand and has the worst network of the three, but they will be cheaper than your foreign sim. Tigo has a good connection at a reasonable price. Vodacom has the best network connection but comes at a cost. If you can afford it, definitely buy a Vodacom sim card.
blocks.html: We suggest Vodacom, Airtel or Tigo. Airtel is the budget option with the weakest network of the three, but it will still cost less than your foreign SIM. Tigo offers a good connection for a fair price. Vodacom has the strongest network but is more expensive. If your budget allows, a Vodacom SIM card is the one to get.

blocks.orig: Although Tanzania is very friendly to tourists, there will always be people ready to catch a holidaymaker.. like in any other country. To make sure you don’t fall victim to muggings, travel at night in groups. Criminals can spot a tourist from a mile away, so don’t take the chance.
blocks.html: Tanzania is very welcoming to tourists, but as in any other country there will always be people looking to take advantage of a holidaymaker. To avoid being mugged, move around in groups at night. Criminals can recognise a tourist from far away, so don’t take the risk.

blocks.orig: This leads us to our next trip. Only carry the essentials you need for the day. If you lose your passport or your visa, you can land in big trouble trying to leave the country.
blocks.html: That brings us to our next tip: carry only what you need for the day. Losing your passport or visa can cause you serious problems when you try to leave the country.

blocks.orig: On the other hand, don’t leave your hotel room without sunscreen and mosquito spray. These sprays will become your best friend as the heat beats down on you.
blocks.html: Then again, never leave your hotel room without mosquito spray and sunscreen. Once the heat hits you, these sprays will be your closest companions.

blocks.orig: This is more general advice than Tanzania specifically. Only take what you need for hiking, lounging, and swimming at the beach. You can buy more clothes when you arrive, and you can wash them at your hotel. Instead, save your bag room for gifts and souvenirs.
blocks.html: This tip applies more broadly than just to Tanzania. Bring only what you need for hiking, relaxing and swimming at the beach. You can buy extra clothes after you arrive and have them washed at your hotel. Keep the space in your bag for gifts and souvenirs instead.

blocks.orig: The lighter you pack the less you have to pay for travel too. To make the most of the savings, buy disposable products when you arrive. Shampoo, travel toothpaste, and other small needed toiletries can be bought anywhere near your hotel, so don’t waste travel space.
blocks.html: Packing light also means paying less for your travel. To save as much as possible, buy disposable items once you arrive. Shampoo, travel toothpaste and other small toiletries are sold everywhere near your hotel, so don’t use up luggage space on them.

blocks.orig: In Tanzania, tipping is the same as breathing. You will be expected to tip around 10 to 12% for basic interactions such as having your picture taken, driving, or being served at a cafe. However, if you are in a fine dining restaurant or a 5-star hotel, the tipping expectancy jumps up to 20%.
blocks.html: Tipping in Tanzania is as natural as breathing. For everyday interactions, such as someone taking your photo, driving you or serving you in a cafe, you are expected to tip about 10 to 12%. In a fine dining restaurant or a 5-star hotel, however, the expected tip rises to 20%.

blocks.orig: You are expected to tip for every interaction, so be sure to count those extra coins before committing to a purchase.
blocks.html: A tip is expected for every interaction, so make sure you count out those extra coins before you agree to a purchase.

blocks.orig: The best places to visit in Tanzania are Mount Kilimanjaro, the Northern Circuit safaris, Lake Victoria or Manyara, the Iraqw Village, and the Arusha Cultural Heritage Center. If you don’t visit at least one of these places on your trip, then you will end up missing the most iconic areas of the county.
blocks.html: The top places to visit in Tanzania are Mount Kilimanjaro, the Northern Circuit safaris, Lake Victoria or Manyara, the Iraqw Village and the Arusha Cultural Heritage Center. Miss all of these on your trip and you will have missed the most iconic parts of the country.

blocks.orig: Remember, as you plan your trip be sure to include days of rest, as the wonderful wildlife can overwhelm a tourist. So don’t forget to soak in the spar days, and relax by the sea.
blocks.html: Finally, when you plan your trip, remember to build in some rest days, as all that wonderful wildlife can be overwhelming. So make time for spa days and for relaxing by the sea.
